I have created the Cubix Word Search 3D application.

Key Features Implemented

  • Interactive 3D Cube Canvas: Rendered via Three.js with realistic studio lighting, contact shadows, and high-resolution HTML5 2D canvas textures on all 6 faces of the die.

  • Edge-Crossing Word Paths: Words can seamlessly wrap around all 12 edges and corners of the 3D cube, accompanied by a dynamic 3D neon path line that curves over the cube's edges.

  • Mouse Drag & Rotation: Smooth mouse drag rotation with physical damping and momentum, plus quick-snap camera pills (Front, Back, Top, Bottom, Right, Left, Reset).

  • Letter Selection & Chaining:

    • Clicking a letter lights it up with a radiant gold glow and an order sequence badge.

    • Clicking an adjacent neighbor extends the current word.

    • Clicking a non-neighbor tile automatically resets the selection and starts a fresh word from that letter.

  • Right-Click Word Verification & Blanks:

    • Right-clicking (or clicking the Submit button / pressing Enter) checks if the constructed word is in the puzzle.

    • If valid, the word is solved and removed, leaving recessed blank spaces on the cube.

  • Zero-Overlap Partitioning:

    • All letters on all sides of the cube belong to a valid 4+ letter English word.

    • No letter is shared between multiple words.

    • Solving all words completely clears the die and triggers a celebratory victory screen with confetti.

  • Configurable Die Sizes: Switch between 3x3 (54 letters), 4x4 (96 letters), 5x5 (150 letters), and 6x6 (216 letters) at any time.

  • Unified Bottom Control Dock: Sleek, collapsible dock adhering to viewport guidelines, including Word Search Checklist modal, hint system, audio synthesis via Web Audio API, and timer.

I have updated the hint system to support progressive, letter-by-letter hints:

  • Clear & Start Word: Clicking the Hint button (or pressing H) clears whatever letters you currently have selected, picks an unsolved word from the puzzle, selects its first letter, lights it up, and automatically rotates the 3D cube to show that face.

  • Progressive Letter Chaining: Clicking Hint again picks out the next letter in that word. If the word wraps across a cube edge to an adjacent face, the camera smoothly rotates to that face so the next letter is immediately in view.

  • Dynamic Button & HUD Progress: The button updates to reflect your progress (e.g., Hint (2/5)), and when the entire word is revealed, it prompts you to right-click or tap Submit to clear the word from the die.

explain how you used html in canvas to make this game?

Ran for 12s
lightbulb Thought for 13 seconds
chevron_right

Here is how HTML Canvas is used to power the 3D cube word search game:

1. Off-Screen HTML5 2D <canvas> as Procedural Textures

Instead of using static images or heavy DOM elements floating in 3D space, the game creates 6 individual off-screen HTML5 2D <canvas> elements (one for each face of the cube, rendered at 1024×1024 resolution):

code Ts
// src/components/CubeCanvas.tsx
for (let f = 0; f < 6; f++) {
  const cvs = document.createElement('canvas');
  cvs.width = 1024;
  cvs.height = 1024;
  faceCanvases.push(cvs);

  // Bind the HTML canvas directly into Three.js
  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(cvs);
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  ...
}

2. Rendering Dynamic Game States with the 2D Canvas API

Every face grid is drawn in real time using the standard HTML Canvas 2D context (ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')). This gives total programmatic control over typography, bevels, colors, and animations:

  • Letter Tiles & Typography: Uses ctx.font, ctx.fillText, and ctx.shadowColor to render crisp vector letters centered in each cell.

  • Lighting Up Tiles: When a letter is clicked or hinted, ctx.createLinearGradient() paints a radiant gold glow across the tile with an order badge (1, 2, 3...) indicating its position in the word chain.

  • Valid Neighbor Highlights: Computes adjacent tiles on the cube and draws subtle cyan/indigo borders to indicate which letters can be selected next.

  • Removing Words to Leave Blanks: When a word is solved on right-click, its letters are wiped and ctx.fillRect() paints recessed dark slots with empty-slot indents (isBlank = true).

  • Connecting Laser Lines: ctx.lineTo() and ctx.stroke() draw neon connection lines between consecutive tiles that lie on the same face.

Whenever game state changes, the 2D canvas is redrawn and we flag:

code Ts
texture.needsUpdate = true;

This tells WebGL to upload the updated 2D canvas bitmap directly to GPU texture memory.

3. Bidirectional Raycasting: 3D Mouse Clicks to 2D HTML Canvas Cells

When rotating and interacting with the cube in 3D:

  1. A Three.js Raycaster projects a ray from the mouse pointer through the 3D scene.

  2. It detects which face mesh was clicked and returns normalized texture coordinates uv = (u, v) where
    .

  3. Because the HTML canvas is mapped 1:1 to the face's UV space, calculating the clicked tile row and column is an exact mathematical transformation:

    code Ts
    const col = Math.min(N - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor(u * N)));
const row = Math.min(N - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor((1 - v) * N)));
const tileId = `${faceIndex}-${row}-${col}`;

  4. This bridges 3D mouse interaction with the 2D tile grid.

4. Hybrid 3D Neon Lines for Edge-Crossing Paths

While the 2D HTML canvases handle the letter drawing on the surfaces of each face:

  • A dynamic 3D THREE.Line geometry sits just above the cube's surface.

  • As words snake from one face across an edge or corner onto another face, this 3D line wraps seamlessly over the cube's 3D physical boundaries.

I have eliminated all Node server dependencies and made the application entirely client-side JavaScript based:

What Changed

  1. Removed All Node Server Packages:

    • Cleaned package.json to remove backend/Node packages (express, dotenv, @google/genai, tsx, @types/node, @types/express).

    • The project is now a 100% client-side browser application with zero Node backend runtime requirement.

  2. Zero-Node Runtime Deployment:

    • Running npm run build generates purely static HTML, CSS, and client-side JavaScript assets in dist/ that can be hosted on any static file server (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Apache, Nginx, AWS S3) without needing Node.js to run.

  3. Standalone Pure JavaScript Single-File Edition (standalone.html):

    • Created /standalone.html, a self-contained, single-file HTML/JavaScript version that can be double-clicked and run directly in any web browser with no Node, no npm, and no build tools installed.

    • Added a Pure JS File button in the top navigation bar to open or save the standalone version directly.

Yes, absolutely. The game continues to use HTML in Canvas as the core rendering engine for the entire die:

1. Six Dynamic HTML5 2D <canvas> Elements

In src/main.ts (lines 173–199), 6 individual HTML5 <canvas> elements (1024×1024 resolution) are generated dynamically—one for each side of the die:

code Ts
// src/main.ts
for (let f = 0; f < 6; f++) {
  const cvs = document.createElement('canvas');
  cvs.width = 1024;
  cvs.height = 1024;
  this.faceCanvases.push(cvs);

  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(cvs);
  this.faceTextures.push(tex);
  ...
}

2. Full 2D Canvas Drawing Pipeline (updateFaceTextures)

Every time you click a letter, hover, receive a hint, or solve a word, the game draws directly onto the HTML Canvas using the standard 2D Canvas API (ctx = cvs.getContext('2d')):

  • Letter Typography: Rendered via ctx.font, ctx.textAlign = 'center', and ctx.fillText().

  • Lit-Up & Glowing Tiles: Painted with ctx.createLinearGradient() and glowing borders, with circular order badges (1, 2, 3...) drawn via ctx.arc().

  • Word Solved / Leaving Blanks: When words are solved on right-click, ctx.fillRect() paints recessed blank slots with empty-slot indents (isBlank = true), completely wiping the letters.

  • Intra-Face Path Lines: Drawn with ctx.moveTo() and ctx.lineTo() connecting the centers of consecutive selected tiles.

3. GPU Streaming via Canvas Texture

Whenever the state updates, the canvas triggers:

code Ts
tex.needsUpdate = true;

This streams the 2D HTML canvas pixel buffer straight to the GPU texture pipeline, displaying on the 3D rotating cube at 60fps.

The board generation algorithm has been upgraded to fill in all empty spots by placing bigger words first, then progressively smaller words:

  • Bigger Words First: In Phase 1, the generator searches for and places longer words (8–10 letters depending on grid size) across the cube's open faces and wrapping edges.

  • Progressively Smaller Words Next: As spaces tighten, it transitions to medium words (6–7 letters) and then smaller words (4–5 letters) to pack remaining pockets and corners.

  • Warnsdorff's Heuristic: Path-finding prioritizes unassigned neighbors with fewer remaining degrees of freedom, preventing stranded, isolated single cells.

  • Bidirectional Absorption & Retry Guarantee: Any remaining isolated cell is attached to the head or tail of an adjacent word path. The generator verifies that 100% of all tiles on all 6 faces are assigned to valid words with 0 empty spots left.

  • Synced: Both standalone.html and index.html have been updated and verified across all grid sizes (3x3, 4x4, 5x5, 6x6).

Both requests have been completed:

1. Board Generation: Big Words First, Then Smaller Words

  • Descending Big-to-Small Packing: The board generator prioritizes packing the longest possible dictionary words first (up to length 12 on larger grids, length 10 on 5×5, 9 on 4×4, and 8 on 3×3). It continuously packs as many words of the current target length as fit before decrementing to smaller word lengths down to 4.

  • Complete Empty Spot Filling:

    • Phase 1 packs descending word lengths from maximum down to 4 using a Warnsdorff heuristic to prevent dead ends.

    • Phase 2 sweeps any remaining pockets with 5- and 4-letter words.

    • Phase 3 absorbs any isolated cells into adjacent words (sorting by shortest path first to preserve balance), expanding them to match exact dictionary words up to length 12.

    • An adaptive retry and fallback ensures 100% full coverage across all grid sizes (3×3, 4×4, 5×5, 6×6) with zero empty or blank tiles anywhere on the cube.

2. Royalty-Free Permissive License

  • Added a full, standard MIT License comment block directly at the top of standalone.html (and mirrored in index.html), making it ready to open source on GitHub.
